findings: Receipt bytes are LF-normalized hash-bound; duplicate normalized paths/content refuse. Input fingerprints are syntax-checked assertions, not recomputed against original mathematical inputs.

Every repeated item requires exactly one explicit resolution. AGREE_OPEN requires same scope/status and all-open observations; SUPERSEDE requires old-open/current-closed, matching status/replacement list and existing replacements. These are declared receipt consistency conditions, not proof checking.
Single-receipt replacement references skip the existence validation applied to resolutions. The synthetic control accepts an absent replacement.
Duplicate open_items pass set equality while record open_count uses list length. Aggregate unique item count stays correct.
Stable ID regex uses match with a dollar anchor and accepts final newline; use fullmatch for consistent IDs.

CLI --emit-review can overwrite its input manifest or bound receipt without a protection check. Unique mkstemp avoids the earlier shared writer temp-name ownership problem, but does not prevent input replacement.

Compact review receipt retains aggregate history/counts but omits item observations; it is not itself an accepted frontier/v1 receipt and is not independently sufficient to recompute the full report fingerprint.
proposed_repairs: Protect manifest and bound source identities before emission, with canonical filesystem alias handling; use explicit existing-output replacement policy.
Reject duplicate open_items and validate member types before set conversion; derive counts from normalized observations.
Apply replacement existence policy consistently to lone and overlapping observations; do not infer mathematical coverage from replacement references.
remaining: Semantic overlap beyond equality of IDs/scope labels is not implemented or validated; retain as an open 0.50 design question.
Replacement cycles and concurrent read/write boundaries remain untested; no broader snapshot guarantee claimed.
